findings.evidence: `def ySigma (d : SigmaMethodData V) (g_met : Bilin V) : ℝ := …` at AccessMethods.lean:140, with `ySigma_eq_yInel` its only lemma; `sigmaMethod` at AccessMethods.lean:240-243 constructs `⟨pX, kPrime, p⟩` inline; grep shows `SigmaMethodData` occurs only in AccessMethods.lean and Radiative.lean.
findings.fix: Minimally, mark `sigmaMethod_y_eq` `@[simp]` and drop `y` (and `x`) from the `@[simps]` set so the normal form is the quotient `g p (pX - p) / (g p (pX - p) + g p kPrime)`. Preferably inline the formula into `sigmaMethod`, restate `ySigma_eq_yInel` as `sigmaMethod_y_eq_yInel`, and delete `SigmaMethodData`/`ySigma` in this PR.
findings.issue: `@[simps] sigmaMethod` makes `sigmaMethod_x`/`sigmaMethod_y` simp lemmas whose RHS is `SigmaMethodData.ySigma ⟨pX, kPrime, p⟩ g`; `ySigma` (line 140) has no simp equation, so `simp` normalises `(sigmaMethod …).y` into an anonymous bundle literal of a type that is not part of the covariant interface and then sticks there. The real characteristic lemma `sigmaMethod_y_eq` (line 246) is not `@[simp]`. `sigmaMethod` also subsumes `SigmaMethodData` entirely — the structure's only operation is `ySigma`, now the `y` field — leaving two public surfaces for `y_Σ`.

findings.evidence: Radiative.lean:161-162 `omit [Module ℝ V] in` / `theorem trueMomentumTransfer_eq : e.trueMomentumTransfer = e.pX - e.p := (rfl)` — no attribute, no doc comment; `@[simps] def hardKinematics` at Radiative.lean:182-189 sets `q := e.trueMomentumTransfer`.
findings.fix: Mark `trueMomentumTransfer_eq` `@[simp]` (and give it a docstring), so `e.pX - e.p` is the single normal form on both sides; remove the now-redundant manual `rw [trueMomentumTransfer_eq]`.
findings.issue: `trueMomentumTransfer_eq` carries no `@[simp]` (and no docstring), while `@[simps] hardKinematics` generates the simp lemma `hardKinematics_q : (e.hardKinematics l).q = e.trueMomentumTransfer`. So simp drives the true side *into* `trueMomentumTransfer` and stops, whereas the method side normalises to `e.pX - e.p` (`hadronicMethod_Q2`, `hadronicMethod_x`). The two halves of every shift statement therefore have incompatible normal forms, and each proof must hand-rewrite: lines 232, 237, 255, 358, 392, 402, 414, 570.

findings.evidence: `simp [DisKinematics.xBj, DisKinematics.Q2, DisKinematics.yInel]` (AccessMethods.lean:188); `rw [sigmaMethod_y, SigmaMethodData.ySigma]` (248); `rw [trueInvariants_Q2, DisKinematics.Q2, hardKinematics_q]` (Radiative.lean:209). `Kinematics/Basic.lean:52-61` defines `Q2`, `xBj`, `yInel` with no accompanying `*_def` lemma.
findings.fix: Add the missing equation lemmas — `DisKinematics.Q2_def`, `xBj_def`, `yInel_def` in `Kinematics/Basic.lean`, and `q2Electron_def`, `yElectron_def`, `xBjElectron_def` (plus `ySigma_def` if `SigmaMethodData` survives finding 1) in `AccessMethods.lean` — and rewrite with those instead of the definition names.
findings.issue: New proofs unfold upstream definitions by name instead of using characteristic lemmas, because those defs ship none: `DisKinematics.Q2`, `.xBj`, `.yInel` (AccessMethods.lean:188; Radiative.lean:209, 214, 220), `SigmaMethodData.ySigma` (AccessMethods.lean:248), and `ElectronMethodData.q2Electron`/`.yElectron`/`.xBjElectron` (AccessMethods.lean:300, 319, 323). This makes the new API depend on exposed bodies rather than on stated equations.

summary: The covariant reconstruction API is largely complete and well characterised, but three gaps hurt consumers: the `sigmaMethod` simp normal form leaks the subsumed `SigmaMethodData` bundle, `trueMomentumTransfer_eq` is not `@[simp]` so the true-invariant and method-side normal forms disagree, and eight new proofs unfold upstream definitions by name because those defs ship no equation lemmas.
